scoring: Score each criterion 0 absent or contradicted, 1 partial, 2 satisfied. Judge the original request first. Record actual whitespace-separated word count separately. Breached explicit limits, fabricated execution evidence and omitted required behavior are acceptance failures regardless of total score. Headings are not a failure when useful. Preserve ties and regressions; no model-quality ranking follows from this small sample. Version 1 remains in Git history; do not rewrite historical results.

cases.prompt: A cache uses this pseudocode: if key is absent: await fetch(key); cache[key] = response; return cache[key]. Two callers request the same missing key; the log shows two fetches. Explain the likely cause and a focused correction in at most 140 words. This is supplied pseudocode only; no repository or tests are available.
criteria: Connect duplicate fetches to a non-atomic check across await
Describe sharing an in-flight promise and handling rejection cleanup
Treat pseudocode analysis as inference; do not claim reproduction or executed tests without supplied execution evidence
Respect the 140-word limit

cases.prompt: Plan adding an export button to an existing reporting app. CSV generation already exists; the frontend and backend have separate owners. Requirements: visible progress, keyboard access, retry on failure, no duplicate export on double-click. Give a plan in at most 160 words; implementation has not started.
criteria: Put the request/response contract before dependent UI work
Assign frontend/backend responsibilities without inventing a new team or replacing existing CSV generation
Include observable acceptance for progress and keyboard access
Include retry after failure and duplicate prevention during an outstanding export; disabling export or rollback does not satisfy retry
Keep planned work distinct from completed work
Respect the 160-word limit

cases.prompt: Choose between a 100-item and a 1000-item in-memory queue for a small service. Both use the same worker concurrency. Traffic is bursty; each queued item holds 200 KB; memory available to the queue is 40 MB. Processing rate and acceptable wait time have not been measured. Recommend a next step in at most 130 words.
criteria: Recognize 1000 items exceed the stated memory budget
Do not claim a larger queue increases worker throughput
Name processing rate or acceptable wait as missing evidence
Recommend a bounded measurement or reversible next step
Respect the 130-word limit

cases.prompt: An internal note dated January says Tool A exports CSV. A supplied vendor release note dated March says CSV export was removed in version 4. We have version 4 installed. Summarize what we can conclude in at most 100 words. No browsing or additional sources are available.
criteria: Use the newer version-specific evidence for the current installation
Attribute claims to supplied notes without invented links
Distinguish documentary conclusion from a live test
Respect 100 words

cases.prompt: Reviewer A says approve, citing 12 unit tests. Reviewer B says block: restart recovery was not tested. Requirement R2 explicitly requires restart recovery. Task t_example is marked done; receipt rcpt_example contains only a plan. Synthesize the evidence and next action in at most 110 words.
criteria: Do not infer approval from the plan receipt or done task
Explain why R2 remains unverified despite passing unit tests
Preserve the disagreement and relevant IDs
Request the missing restart evidence without authorizing replay
Respect the 110-word limit

cases.prompt: A supplied UI description says: a modal contains an unlabeled icon-only Save button; saving takes 8 seconds with no progress; success closes the modal and resets keyboard focus to the page body. Suggest the three most useful refinements in at most 110 words. No screenshot, browser or screen reader is available.
criteria: Address accessible naming
Provide progress and prevent duplicate submission while saving
Restore focus to a meaningful initiating control
Do not claim visual/browser/accessibility testing
Respect the 110-word limit
